case.description: Create a reusable joint between two square rods in a tabletop pointer frame. The joint must let the operator exchange either rod while restoring the pointer's marked position without altering the rods.
case.valued_outcome: After five exchanges of each rod, the pointer returns within a 2 mm target circle and remains there during a supplied 10 N lateral load for ten seconds; each exchange takes less than forty seconds.
hard_constraints: No drilling, adhesive or permanent marks on either rod.
Joint envelope must fit inside a 90 mm cube.
Only hand-operated assembly and adjustment are permitted.
No component may fall free during an exchange.
resources: Two 400 mm square rods, measured sides 19 mm and 20 mm, plus one pointer and marked base.
Six plywood pieces each 80 by 40 by 6 mm, eight M5 bolts with nuts, four washers, two 150 mm elastic loops and 0.5 m of cord.
Hand drill for plywood only, saw, file, screwdriver and ruler.
One hundred minutes for fabrication and twenty minutes for testing.
observations: The current loose joint lets the pointer move 7 mm under the load.
Rod ends are square within the supplied 1 mm measurement resolution.
Awkward observation: the visually tighter rod fit returned 3 mm farther from the target after exchange than the looser fit in two supplied trials.

openings.claim: Registration against fixed faces and an insertion stop, followed by clamping, could restore position more consistently than maximizing visible tightness.
openings.delta: Change the joint's locating carrier to plywood corner seats with fixed end-stop tabs for both rods. Adjustable bolt clamps press each rod toward the same two faces; rod width changes clamp travel rather than the locating faces. Cord and elastic keepers must retain every movable part before either rod is released.
openings.prediction: Compared with a tighter fit in the same carrier, deliberate seating before clamping predicts smaller exchange-return errors, including with the 18 mm rod. The nearest rival is that overall tightness determines repeatability and the two awkward trials were incidental. That rival predicts the tighter configuration does at least as well; equal results would not discriminate.
openings.probe: Use at most two configurations of the same adjustable carrier: deliberate datum seating with sufficient clamping, and increased tightness. Per configuration, exchange each original rod five times, then substitute the 18 mm rod for the final two exchanges in the smaller-rod seat: twelve exchanges total. Record target displacement and exchange time after each. Apply four ten-second 10 N lateral trials after exchanges 5, 10, 11 and 12, recording position throughout. A useful result requires both a configuration difference beyond ruler resolution and assessment against the 2 mm, forty-second and loaded-position requirements. Do not deploy from this probe.
assumptions: The unspecified frame geometry permits both seats and stops within 90 mm.
Available bolt lengths, plywood stiffness and keeper reach permit adjustable, captive clamps; these are unverified indispensable capacities.
Fabrication must fit 100 minutes and the complete comparison 20 minutes; schedule feasibility is unproven.

Defeat conditions include insufficient clamp travel, loose stop attachment, plywood crushing, load slip, or any untethered component. If resources cannot provide captivity or adequate load resistance, reject this construction without relaxing constraints.

artifact.assessment: A testable candidate, with no claimed fabrication or performance. The supplied return anomaly motivates decoupling location from clamping but does not establish its cause.

openings.claim: Speculative capability: a deliberately clearance-rich joint could restore the pointer more repeatably than a visually tight joint while accommodating the 18 mm replacement. Repeatability would come from seating order, rather than matching rod width.
openings.delta: Change the dependency from opposed tight-fit contacts to the same two adjacent plywood datum faces and an insertion stop for each rod. Change the action to end-stop contact, corner seating, then hand tightening. The carrier is a shared plywood cradle with bolt-operated restraint; elastic loops supply seating bias and cord retains releasable hardware. Cut and drill only plywood. Keep both rod pockets and all retained hardware inside the 90 mm cube.
openings.prediction: Nearest rival: tighter symmetric restraint improves both stiffness and return. The seating-order hypothesis predicts the datum configuration has smaller post-exchange displacement despite visible clearance, including after substitution; the rival predicts tight-fit superiority. If return errors improve but loaded drift increases, repeatability and restraint remain separate unresolved dependencies. The two supplied trials suggest a discriminator, not proof.
openings.probe: Use the six plywood pieces, eight bolts and nuts, four washers, loops, cord and permitted hand tools to fabricate one captive cradle within 100 minutes. Compare two configurations: datum seating before tightening versus opposed tightening using the same hardware. Before timed exchanges, verify envelope and that loosened hardware stays attached. Within 20 testing minutes, allocate twelve exchanges and four 10 N, ten-second load trials per configuration: five exchanges per original rod followed by two 18 mm substitutions. Record exchange time, target-card return, loaded displacement and retention. Counterbalance configuration order. Stop if retention fails; a stopped run establishes no performance success.
assumptions: The required rod orientation permits both pockets within the envelope; orientation is unspecified.
Available plywood and bolts can form sufficiently rigid datums, and cord can securely retain hardware without obstructing removal; verify before exchanges.

Defeat conditions include worse return than the rival, target escape under load, any exchange reaching forty seconds, loose components, or exhausted fabrication/testing time. Insufficient measurement resolution or incomplete trials leave the outcome unresolved.
No drilling, adhesive or permanent rod marks are permitted; preload must avoid permanent indentation. This is an enabling experiment, not deployment.

artifact.assessment: One opening. Seating discrimination is possible with stipulated resources; stiffness, captive retention, orientation compatibility and sufficient test time remain unproved.

openings.claim: Separate seating from restraint: plywood-derived corner datums and an axial stop locate each rod; hand-operated M5 pressure members then press it into those datums. Tether movable members and nuts with cord, using loops for retention. This is a construction candidate, not demonstrated performance.
openings.delta: Change the dependency from tight enclosing clearance to deliberate datum seating before clamping. The nearest rival is a tighter enclosing fit that restrains movement but may trap the rod before it reaches its stop.
openings.prediction: If incomplete seating explains the supplied reversal, datum-first seating should reduce unloaded return error versus enclosing contact; tightening may improve loaded stability without improving return error. If both configurations seat equally yet return similarly, that explanation loses support. The 18 mm substitution may expose centerline or pointer-offset dependence despite repeatable face seating.
openings.probe: Within the six plywood pieces, fabricate one reversible fixture with corner/stop contact and optional enclosing contact; use only supplied fasteners and tools. First verify retained components, hand access, 90 mm envelope and achievable fastening geometry. Compare two configurations with five exchanges of each original rod followed by two 18 mm substitutions each. Record exchange duration and unloaded pointer error. Use four ten-second 10 N trials per configuration, covering initial assembly, fifth exchange of each original rod and final substitution. Record target escape during loading. At forty seconds per exchange, only 160 seconds remain for switching, load setup and logging within twenty minutes; infeasible timing leaves the comparison unresolved.
assumptions: Required rod orientation and pointer attachment permit fixed face datums; neither is supplied.
Plywood subdivisions, eight bolts, four washers, loops and cord can realize adequately stiff, captive pressure members inside the envelope within 100 minutes; this requires verification.

Defeat conditions include inconsistent stop contact, contact crushing, clamp slip, angular amplification beyond 2 mm, substitution-dependent offset, loose components, or exchanges exceeding forty seconds.
Two adverse trials motivate a seating hypothesis but do not establish its cause.

artifact.assessment: Informative if both contact configurations and measurement timing are realizable. Feasibility and the complete loaded-return outcome remain unproven; no deployment follows from this probe.
